statement: Universal preservation of a specified class W by strict pullback is stable under composition and arbitrary base change; restricted contractible-base tests differ.
notes: No two-out-of-three assumption on W is needed for formal stability.

statement: A universal weak fibration pulls back a 1-complete base equivalence to a constant equivalence; all-local-coefficients direct images yield composable cohomological fibrations.
depends_on: A inclusion chain; C.2 for enhanced equality
notes: The conclusion is not silently upgraded to Wlc. The dual homological argument is included.

statement: Universal weak rational fibrations do not compose, with an explicit two-object/four-object categorical counterexample.
depends_on: exact invariants of finite groups over Q
notes: Five arrows in intermediate category; ten in total; endpoint fibre component counts 2 and1.

statement: The manuscript restricted 2-complete fibration class fails composition even for sets and finite categories.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms122 composition development; Lead3 blanket substitution
notes: Nonzero normalized C2 cocycle on barycentric S2; all categorical laws and pi1 presentations checked.

statement: Total-to-fibre equivalence fails for the blanket Wlc and W1 substitutions, although enhanced W1 detection holds for genuine HOT structural fibrations.
notes: Counterexamples include a completely Set-aspherical base and a contractible base respectively.

statement: For an accessible Wlc fundamental localizer, its associated Thomason model fibrations are base-change/composition stable and detect total Wlc equivalences on fibres.
notes: Right properness unnecessary for the slice-fibrant fibre-detection assertion; model fibrations not identified with all sharp maps.

statement: A universal constant-coefficient derivator equivalence induces fully faithful restriction on all coefficients.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I-b-B084-01; I ms82 arbitrary inverse-image fibre formula
notes: Full factorization-category mate proof, including infinite or empty hom-sets.

statement: All HOT equivalence classes coincide, its fibration tests coincide with sharp maps, and Der3 a-prime proves the weak-condition equivalence for general derivators.
depends_on: Cisinski2009 Corollary3.8; Quillen1973 TheoremB; Rezk1998 Proposition2.7
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I-b-B096-04; Ib-C021; Ib-C026; Ib-C048; Ib-C069; Ib-C092; Ib-C096; XI opening
notes: General derivator argument provided separately from HOT identification.

statement: Six auxiliary errors in the manuscript survive changing coefficients: uniqueness, two quotient implications, orbit relations, properness-implies-transport, and internal-Hom implication.
notes: Corrected orbit compositions and quotient rational Betti vector (1,0,0,1) are checked.

statement: The specified doubled-arrow construction cannot fail in HOT; strengthened Wlc and W1 gluing holds for complete enhanced coefficients.
depends_on: homotopy pushout of simplicial monomorphisms; C.1
notes: One specified fork base change; no claim that all base changes preserve the original weak condition.

statement: For every Der1-4 derivator, Wlc and W1 cosieve gluing for the specified doubled-arrow construction holds.
depends_on: B.3 arbitrary-derivator relative Theorem A; B.5 direct excision; Cisinski2006 Theorems1.4.3 and4.2.15
notes: The former general descent gap is resolved. Wlc gluing uses the accessible fundamental sublocalizer generated by the single cosieve inclusion; no accessibility assumption on all Wlc is needed. W1 uses B.5 Loc6a.

statement: Universal weak fibrations for set coefficients need not preserve constant equivalences, refuting the manuscript's 0-type qualification.
notes: e→BC2 preserves pi0; pullback G_disc→EG changes pi0.
